title: Juan Claver’s cipher letter from Milan

steps.what: Alberto Garvía García matched the symbols with Parisi’s published table for the Ferdinand–Escrivà correspondence.
Filed the issue evidence and checked the line replay against the submitted transcription and key.

Page review: rewrote the write-up from NOTES.md, profile.json and key.tsv. Rechecked the sign counts (437 signs, 390 P, 44 V, 3 U) against transcription.tsv and key.tsv, and marked word starts in the reveal file against cipher-reading.md. Not rechecked against the manuscript images, and no prior publication of this passage was searched for.

outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: Alberto Garvía García matched the symbols with Parisi’s published table for the Ferdinand–Escrivà correspondence.
outcome.fraction_read_source: 100 of 104 cipher words sure (cipher-reading.md, prior review; 99 of 104 if the anomalous 'sopiendo' counts as a hole). Signs, a separate measure: 437 signs in transcription.tsv, 434 valued (390 matching the printed form, 44 provisional) and 3 unresolved (G31, G40, G42), plus a tear of about two signs.

texts.summary: The enciphered passage of Juan Claver's letter from Milan to the Catholic Monarchs: reports on the French king, the archduke and the King of the Romans, and on troops leaving a place in Burgundy.

reading_review.by: Codex independent claims review, Claver and Latin
reading_review.note: The Spanish cipher block and English translation are coherent with scattered holes. The review reproduced all 11 aligned lines and counted 437 cipher signs. Earlier review sampled the manuscript; this review used the committed transcriptions and explicit sign-doubt record.

texts.label: The cipher passage of the letter of 19 June 1497

gaps.item: three unresolved signs and lacuna at the tear

human: The contributors supplied their transcription, key and reading.
